cases.question:
Optum is a global organization that delivers care, aided by technology to help millions of people live healthier lives. The work you do with our team will directly improve health outcomes by connecting people with the care, pharmacy benefits, data and resources they need to feel their best. Here, you will find a culture guided by inclusion, talented peers, comprehensive benefits and career development opportunities. Come make an impact on the communities we serve as you help us advance health optimization on a global scale. Join us to start Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

We are looking for an ML Engineer with solid hands-on experience in GenAI and agentic frameworks, backed by solid foundational ML/NLP knowledge. The role involves building production-grade AI systems across verticals such has Health, Rx, Productization etc.

Primary Responsibilities:

Build and deploy GenAI and agentic AI solutions in production environments
Design ML systems involving structured/unstructured data and complex database interactions
Develop scalable Python-based ML pipelines and APIs
Work on foundational ML use cases including prediction, optimization, and recommendation systems
Collaborate with product, engineering, and platform teams to operationalize models
Take lead in productionizing models including API design and integration, load testing, HPC compute, Latency management
Comply with the terms and conditions of the employment contract, company policies and procedures, and any and all directives (such as, but not limited to, transfer and/or re-assignment to different work locations, change in teams and/or work shifts, policies in regard to flexibility of work benefits and/or work environment, alternative work arrangements, and other decisions that may arise due to the changing business environment). The Company may adopt, vary or rescind these policies and directives in its absolute discretion and without any limitation (implied or otherwise) on its ability to do so
Required Qualifications:

Master's or preferably PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related field
Solid foundation in machine learning, deep learning, and statistical modeling
Hands-on experience with NLP, LLMs, transformers, and generative AI techniques
Experience with building and orchestrating AI agents or multi-agent systems
Experience working with large-scale datasets and distributed computing (e.g., Spark/PySpark)
Proficiency in Python and ML frameworks/libraries (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn)
Understanding of model optimization techniques (e.g., FLOPs reduction, quantization, latency tuning)
Familiarity with MLOps practices, model deployment, and monitoring in production environments
Knowledge of APIs, microservices architecture, and system integration
Solid problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment
At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and make the health system work better for everyone. We believe everyone - of every race, gender, sexuality, age, location and income - deserves the opportunity to live their healthiest life. Today, however, there are still far too many barriers to good health which are disproportionately experienced by people of color, historically marginalized groups and those with lower incomes. We are committed to mitigating our impact on the environment and enabling and delivering equitable care that addresses health disparities and improves health outcomes - an enterprise priority reflected in our mission.

response.headline: Partial fit for Optum’s ML Engineer role
response.summary: Rakshit is highly relevant to GenAI product prototyping, RAG, agentic workflows, evals, Python-based AI apps, and cross-functional AI delivery. The gap is that this Optum role is an ML Engineer position with hard requirements around advanced ML education, distributed computing, model optimization, MLOps, latency/load/HPC productionization, and likely deeper engineering ownership than the profile proves.
response.answerText:
Rakshit is a strong adjacent candidate for Optum’s GenAI/agentic AI direction, but only a partial fit for this specific ML Engineer role.

The strongest match is on applied GenAI systems: he has built LLM products involving RAG, semantic search, tool-calling agents, evaluation frameworks, and Python-based AI prototypes. His ET Money support automation work is especially relevant because it translated ambiguous support problems into intent classification, 100+ resolution workflows, and evals, reducing monthly support tickets from 17,000 to 7,000.

He also has hands-on agentic evidence: AI Hiring Chat uses a multi-stage agent pipeline for URL detection, company research, context selection, and structured fit assessment; Feedback Intelligence and US Stocks Analysis Agent evidence show tool calling, specialist handoffs, persistent memory, and improved tool-use accuracy from 58% to 90%.

Where the fit drops is the engineering depth required by the JD. The role asks for production ML engineering: Spark/PySpark, large-scale datasets, distributed compute, PyTorch/TensorFlow/scikit-learn, model optimization such as quantization/FLOPs/latency tuning, MLOps monitoring, load testing, HPC compute, and API/microservice integration. Rakshit has Python, FastAPI, Streamlit, ChromaDB, embeddings, OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, and deployable AI product experience, but the profile does not prove deep ML engineering ownership at Optum’s expected scale. He also does not meet the stated Master’s/PhD preference based on the available education evidence.

He would be more directly positioned for Optum as an AI Product Manager, GenAI Product Lead, AI Solutions PM, or applied AI prototyping/productization role. For this ML Engineer opening, he could still be valuable if the team needs someone who can bridge product, LLM workflows, evals, and rapid prototypes with engineering teams—but not if the role is primarily deep ML infrastructure and model optimization.

cases.question:
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager who brings genuine depth in Voice AI or BFSI, and the execution muscle to turn complex enterprise problems into products that actually get used. In this role, you won’t just be shipping features. You will be leading a product charter within one of the most consequential applications of AI in Indian financial services.

As a senior member of a lean, fast-moving team, you will own your charter end-to-end, from discovery through delivery and adoption. You will work directly with enterprise customers, founders, and engineering to define what our AI platform does next, and be accountable for the outcomes, not just the output.

Location: Mumbai / Bengaluru

What You’ll Do
1. Domain Depth: BFSI or Voice AI
Know your domain: You bring meaningful depth in at least one of two worlds. Either the BFSI industry (how banks, NBFCs, fintechs, and insurance companies actually operate, where their workflows break down, and what compliance and operations teams really care about) or Voice AI products (how conversational AI systems are built, deployed, and fail at scale; the difference between a bot that handles volume and one that handles nuance). Either gives you a head start that matters.

Translate domain into product: You can take a messy enterprise requirement, buried in regulatory language, competing stakeholder asks, and legacy process assumptions, and distill it into a clean product opportunity with a clear north star. Your domain knowledge makes you faster at this, not more rigid.

Bridge the gap: Wherever your depth starts, you close the other side quickly. You understand that Voice AI only creates real value in BFSI when you understand both, and you’re genuinely curious about whichever world is newer to you.

2. Charter Ownership & Cross-Functional Execution
Own a product area: Lead a focused charter, whether that’s a specific use case vertical (collections, servicing, onboarding), a platform capability (analytics, integrations, configurability), or an enterprise workflow. You set the vision, own the roadmap, and are accountable for outcomes, not just delivery.

Enterprise discovery: Run structured discovery with CXOs, operations heads, and compliance teams. Navigate competing stakeholder inputs without losing the thread, and surface insights that become product decisions, not slide decks.

Ship and drive adoption: Manage delivery across engineering, QA, and customer success. Features that go live but don’t get used aren’t shipped. You’re not done until they’re embedded in customer workflows and generating measurable value.

Go-to-market partnership: Work closely with sales and solutions teams during pre-sales, pilots, and expansion. Your product knowledge should be a competitive asset in enterprise conversations, not something that stays inside the building.

3. Product Instinct & Domain Judgment
As AI compresses the time to build, the ability to deeply know the customer, and separate what they actually need from what they ask for, becomes the rarest and most valuable PM skill.

Anticipate, don’t just respond: The best product decisions at GreyLabs won’t come from feature requests. They’ll come from someone who understands the customer deeply enough to see around corners. Whether that instinct is built from years inside BFSI or years shipping voice AI products, you should be able to walk into a room and identify the real problem before anyone has named it.

Opinionated prioritisation: You have a clear point of view on what matters and what doesn’t. You can push back on a customer request that would create technical debt without strategic value, say no to a feature that solves one account’s edge case, and explain why in terms the account team and the customer will respect.

Quality as a habit: You hold a high bar for what “done” means. A feature that’s live but not adopted, or a workflow that works in the demo but breaks in production, is not done. You define success criteria before you start, and you follow through until they’re met.

4. Ambiguity & Growth
Voice AI in Indian BFSI is not a mature category. The use cases, the regulation, and the customer expectations are still being written. You should be energised by that, comfortable holding a strong opinion while remaining genuinely open to being wrong, and disciplined about evolving your thinking as the market does.

What We’re Looking For
6+ years of product management experience: with a track record of owning a product area end-to-end in a B2B SaaS or enterprise environment. You’ve led charters, not just contributed to them.

Deep domain expertise in BFSI or Voice AI: A genuine track record in at least one: meaningful experience building for or within financial services (banking, NBFC, fintech, insurance) or substantial experience owning and shipping voice or conversational AI products. Both are learnable. Just not both from scratch, at the same time, in a fast-moving startup.

Enterprise execution: You’ve managed complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise rollouts where success means adoption and workflow change, not just deployment. You understand what it actually takes to get a bank to change how it operates.

AI curiosity with some proof: You’ve worked on, shipped, or meaningfully engaged with an AI product, professionally or otherwise. You understand the fundamental difference between AI-driven and rule-based products, and have opinions about it.

Clear, direct communicator: You write and speak with precision. A Chief Collections Officer in the morning, a backend engineer in the afternoon. You adapt fluently between both.

response.headline: Relevant fit for GreyLabs AI Senior PM, strongest on fintech + AI execution; enterprise Voice AI depth is the main gap
response.summary: Rakshit is meaningfully aligned with GreyLabs’ BFSI Voice AI direction through 5+ years in fintech, AI support automation, lending/wealth/insurance product ownership, and hands-on voice/agentic AI prototypes. The fit is not “Strong” because the role asks for 6+ years, deep enterprise Voice AI or BFSI operations depth, and bank/NBFC rollout experience; the profile has adjacent but not fully direct evidence there.
response.answerText:
Rakshit would be a relevant fit for this Senior Product Manager role, especially if GreyLabs values a PM who can combine fintech product judgment with hands-on AI prototyping and outcome ownership.

His strongest match is the intersection of fintech workflows and AI execution. At ET Money, he built AI support automation with intent classification, 100+ resolution workflows, and evals for empathy, answer quality, policy compliance, and regression testing, reducing monthly tickets from 17,000 to 7,000. That maps well to GreyLabs’ need for products that go beyond demos and drive operational adoption.

He also has credible BFSI-adjacent depth across lending, wealth, insurance, mutual funds, and advisory products: Loan Against Mutual Funds scaled to INR 100Cr disbursals in 7 months, ET Money Earn reached INR 300Cr AUM, and insurance revenue doubled from INR 1.5Cr to INR 3Cr. This gives him strong financial-services product context, though the evidence is more fintech/consumer-finance/product-platform oriented than bank-operations, collections, compliance, or enterprise BFSI workflow transformation.

On Voice AI, he has hands-on but not enterprise-scale evidence. He built a US Stocks Analysis Agent with voice input via Whisper and spoken responses via TTS, and made a product tradeoff to simplify the voice path because latency matters more in spoken interfaces. He also built an AI Evaluation Framework that measures ASR quality using WER/CER, including language and speaking-style comparisons. That is relevant for GreyLabs’ Voice AI platform, but it is not the same as owning production conversational AI for collections, telesales, servicing, or compliance at bank/NBFC scale.

The key calibration: Rakshit fits the spirit of a lean AI product builder who can own ambiguous problems, prototype fast, define evals, and ship measurable fintech outcomes. The risk is seniority and enterprise depth: the JD asks for 6+ years, end-to-end charter ownership in B2B SaaS/enterprise, and multi-stakeholder enterprise rollouts with CXOs, ops heads, compliance, sales/solutions, and customer success. The profile shows strong product execution, but not enough direct evidence of enterprise customer discovery and rollout ownership in the exact GreyLabs environment.

Company Overview:



GreyOrange technology specializes in bringing warehouses, distribution centers, and fulfillment centers into the future. Our AI-driven GreyMatterTM Fulfillment Operating System and RangerTM robot series are a combined solution that continuously prioritize decisions and workflows to efficiently orchestrate tasks, time, teams of people and robots for optimum performance across a distribution center. Real-time data fed into always-solving algorithms calculate each next-best decision – for every-day performance and in peak periods. The result is a fast, agile, and precise operation that equips customers to continuously meet the what-when-where expectations of their customers in the most optimal manner possible.


Key Responsibilities:

Code critical sections and key features of the product
Lead and solve key technical challenges in the overall system

Rearchitect existing algorithms & implementations
Perform code reviews and healthy peer feedback to the team
Mentor and guide team members technically

Work with simulations for functional performance
Keep an eye out for technology trends, open-source projects that can be used
Understanding business requirements and converting them into product features

B.E/ B.Tech/M.E/M.Tech/ M.S from a premier institute.
6+ years of work experience, having demonstrated problem solving skills. Have experience designing and implementing non-trivial software systems (e.g., using multiple processes/threads/IPC etc.)
Development experience using Java, Python, Golang, Erlang (either of these)


Good to Have

Exposure to serverless technologies
Exposure to various databases and associated technologies like Postgre sql, Redis etc.

GCP, Azure Cloud etc.).

cases.question:
As an Associate Product Head at MagicBricks, you will play a crucial role in leading the development and execution of innovative consumer internet product strategies to drive business growth and enhance customer experiences. Your focus on data-driven decision-making, user-centric design, and cross-functional collaboration will be key to your success.

**Key Responsibilities:**
- **Product Strategy and Development:**
  - Drive the product vision, strategy, and roadmap to enhance customer experiences and business outcomes.
  - Identify market opportunities, customer needs, and trends in the consumer internet space to create impactful solutions.

- **Team Leadership:**
  - Lead and mentor a team of at least 4 product managers, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence.
  - Provide clear direction, set goals, and monitor team performance to ensure project delivery aligns with business objectives.

- **Cross-functional Collaboration:**
  - Work closely with engineering, design, marketing, and data analytics teams to define and prioritize product requirements.
  - Partner with senior stakeholders to align product initiatives with overall business goals.

- **Customer Focus:**
  - Leverage data insights, customer feedback, and user research to make informed decisions and continuously improve product performance.

cases.question:
Senior AI Product Manager, Logistics Intelligence Platform

About FreightGrid
FreightGrid is a Series B enterprise SaaS company building the operating system
for mid-market freight forwarders and 3PLs. Our platform handles shipment
visibility, customs documentation, and exception management for 200+ enterprise
customers across North America and Europe, including 4 of the top 20 global
3PLs. We've raised $48M from Tier-1 enterprise investors and are scaling our
AI capabilities to move from a system-of-record to a system-of-intelligence.

Location: New York or San Francisco. Hybrid, 3 days/week in office.

The Role
We're hiring a Senior AI Product Manager to own our AI roadmap across the
platform. You'll partner with our ML engineering team to ship AI-native
features — document extraction, exception prediction, shipment ETA models,
and agentic workflows for ops teams. This is a senior IC role reporting to
the VP Product.

What You'll Own
- The AI product roadmap end-to-end. Discovery, prioritization, shipping,
  measurement, iteration.
- Pricing and packaging for AI features. Our customers pay $80K-$400K ACV;
  AI features are increasingly the wedge in renewal conversations.
- Customer discovery with VP Operations, Director of Logistics, and Customs
  Compliance leaders at enterprise accounts. You'll be on 8-10 customer calls
  per week, often alongside our enterprise AEs.
- Working with our ML team on model selection, eval design, and ship/no-ship
  decisions. We expect you to have an opinion on prompt engineering, RAG
  architecture, and when fine-tuning is worth the cost.
- GTM enablement for AI features. You'll write the enablement decks, partner
  with marketing on positioning, and join key sales cycles when needed.

What We're Looking For
- 6+ years of product management experience, with at least 3 years shipping
  enterprise B2B SaaS products to customers paying $50K+ ACV.
- Direct experience selling into or shipping for the logistics, supply chain,
  freight, or adjacent enterprise verticals. Strong preference for candidates
  who have worked with 3PLs, freight forwarders, or large shippers.
- Hands-on experience shipping AI/ML features in production — not just
  "exposure to AI." You should be able to walk us through a specific AI
  feature you scoped, shipped, and measured.
- Experience navigating enterprise sales cycles. You understand procurement,
  legal review, security questionnaires, and the difference between a
  champion and an economic buyer.
- Comfort with ambiguity. Our roadmap shifts quarter to quarter as we learn
  from enterprise design partners.

Nice to Have
- Prior experience at a Series B-D enterprise SaaS company that scaled
  through the $10M-$50M ARR range.
- Technical background — CS degree or significant engineering experience.
  You don't need to code production systems, but you should be able to
  read code and have technical conversations with ML engineers.
- Familiarity with enterprise data platforms (Snowflake, Databricks) and
  modern AI infrastructure (LangChain, vector databases, OpenAI/Anthropic
  APIs).

Compensation
$200K-$260K base, equity, full benefits. Visa sponsorship available for
exceptional candidates.

To Apply
Send your resume, a brief note on the most ambitious AI feature you've
shipped, and one customer story that demonstrates your enterprise PM
chops to careers@freightgrid.io.
